capabilities.name: Required Workflows
capabilities.description: Organization/enterprise-enforced workflows that must pass on targeted repositories, defined via rulesets.
valueProposal: Enforce generalized checks across many repositories from a central place — the workflow can live in another repo or even another org in the same enterprise.

capabilities.name: Reusable Workflows
capabilities.description: Centrally-defined workflows referenced by many repositories to standardize CI/CD.
valueProposal: Streamline common CI/CD tasks across an org or enterprise.
Enforce consistency, reduce duplication, and improve maintainability across many projects.
Allows for an innersourcing model to CI/CD

capabilities.name: GitHub Agentic Workflows (gh-aw)
capabilities.description: AI-powered GitHub Actions workflows (authored in Markdown, compiled to lock files) that reason, adapt, and act autonomously.
valueProposal: **Intelligent, autonomous DevOps:** Bring the power of AI to CI/CD by having intelligence meet automation, extending what's possible with GitHub Actions
**Built-in security and guardrails:** `safe-outputs` separate agent-compute from resource manpulation in a safe and secure way
**Easy and efficient creation and maintenance:** 'Vibe-code' a new agentic workflow from scratch instead of hand-writing YAML by using the custom agent and CLI

capabilities.name: Code Quality
capabilities.description: Automated code-quality analysis with findings surfaced in PRs and fixable via Copilot Autofix.
valueProposal: **Ensure Reliability, Maintainability, and Compliance:** Code Quality gives organizations a single GitHub-native solution to monitor, enforce, and report on code quality and compliance across every repository — helping ensure every line of code, human- or AI-generated, meets the highest standards of reliability, maintainability, and compliance.

**AI-Powered Backlog Analysis & Autofix**: It integrates AI-powered analysis with CodeQL static analysis on the main branch repository backlog, not in pull requests; PRs surface code-quality findings and automated autofix suggestions to accelerate remediation.

**Consistent Enforcement & Merge Gates:** Code Quality enables setting rule sets and merge gates to block pull requests that fail quality standards, supporting consistent enforcement across repositories and organizations.

**Organization-wide Visibility & Governance:** GitHub Code Quality provides organization-wide visibility, governance, and enforcement of code quality standards, helping prevent degradation of maintainability, reliability, and coverage in codebases.

**Simplified Tooling & Developer Experience:** The product reduces complexity by consolidating code quality tooling into a single GitHub-native solution, improving developer experience by minimizing context switching and providing integrated dashboards and reporting.

capabilities.name: Code Coverage
capabilities.description: Test coverage reports uploaded from CI to GitHub Code Quality, shown on pull requests and enforceable through a rule.
valueProposal: **Native Coverage Reporting:** Cobertura reports uploaded with `actions/upload-code-coverage` surface coverage directly in GitHub, replacing third-party services such as Codecov or Coveralls.
**Coverage on Every Pull Request:** Reviewers see the coverage change against `main` and which changed lines are not covered by tests.
**Enforceable Minimums:** The `Restrict code coverage` rule can block pull requests that drop below a coverage threshold.

**All Backends:** Node.js, Java, Python, and PHP CI workflows each upload a report labeled `code-coverage/<backend>-api`; report formats are configured in the test frameworks (Vitest, JaCoCo, pytest-cov, PHPUnit) rather than inline CLI flags.

capabilities.name: Repository Code Quality Insights
capabilities.description: Per-repository dashboard surfacing a quality grade and top violations by category — giving developers and tech leads an at-a-glance health snapshot without reviewing individual alerts.
valueProposal: **At-a-glance Quality Health**: A quality grade summarises the overall health of the repository so any stakeholder can understand the current state instantly without reading through individual alerts.
**Top Issues by Category**: Insights surface the most impactful rule violations by category (reliability, maintainability, security smells), guiding prioritization of technical-debt reduction.

capabilities.name: Organization Code Quality Insights
capabilities.description: Org-level dashboard aggregating code quality grades and metrics across all repositories, enabling engineering leaders to identify high-risk codebases and track remediation at scale.
valueProposal: **Cross-Repository Quality Overview**: Roll up quality grades and top violations across all repositories into a single dashboard, eliminating per-repo navigation for engineering managers.
**Risk Prioritisation at Scale**: Identify which repositories carry the most technical debt and allocate remediation effort where it matters most.

capabilities.name: CodeQL
capabilities.description: Static analysis that detects vulnerabilities in existing code and in pull requests, with default and advanced setups.
valueProposal: **Early Vulnerability Detection:** GitHub Code Scanning helps developers prevent vulnerabilities by detecting them early in the development process, improving code security and developer experience.
**Semantic Code Analysis with CodeQL:** It uses CodeQL’s semantic analysis to precisely detect vulnerabilities, track data flow, and reduce false positives, finding issues other tools may miss.

**Centralized Security Visibility:** The solution provides a unified view of active repositories, alerts, and vulnerability types, enabling prioritization and tracking of remediation progress across the organization.

capabilities.name: Copilot Autofix
capabilities.description: AI-generated remediations for code scanning alerts, built into the platform and surfaced naturally at the PR.
valueProposal: Autofix is built into the platform using Copilot — it doesn't just flag the path/data-flow, it proposes the fix.
Becomes part of the developer workflow naturally at the PR.

capabilities.name: AI Code Scanning (Preview)
capabilities.description: AI-powered code scanning that surfaces findings beyond traditional CodeQL rules, inline in PRs (works best with the PHP backend).
valueProposal: Surfaces security findings in programming languages which are not natively supported by Code-Scanning and its CodeQL rules, expanding our security offering.

capabilities.name: GitHub MCP Security Scanning
capabilities.description: The GitHub Remote MCP Server's security toolsets (dependency + secret scanning) brought into Copilot Agent mode / CLI for pre-commit checks.
valueProposal: Security findings are most valuable while developers are still editing — before CI or PR checks become the first line of defense.
Identify a vulnerable dependency change and recommend a safer version against the Advisory Database without pushing first.
Find exposed credentials in local changes (file + line) before commit, keeping secrets out of Git history.
Keeps security feedback in the same chat-driven workflow where code is being changed.

capabilities.name: Security Campaigns
capabilities.description: Bulk organization of code scanning alerts into a campaign for coordinated remediation, including assignment to Coding Agents.
valueProposal: Allows to bring focus into cleaning-up motions by limitting the scope of alerts
Creates a natively integrated collaboration surfce between security-teams and developers
Speeds up remediation by allowing to assign alerts to Coding Agents for automatic fixes

capabilities.name: GitHub Codespaces
capabilities.description: Cloud-hosted development environments that spin up in seconds, giving you a full VS Code experience in the browser or locally.
valueProposal: **Instant Dev Environments** - Go from repository to ready-to-code environment in seconds, no local setup required.
**Consistent Team Experience** - Prebuilt configurations ensure everyone has the same tools, dependencies, and extensions.
**Cloud Power, Local Feel** - Run resource-intensive builds and tests in the cloud while maintaining familiar IDE workflows.

capabilities.name: GitHub Copilot App
capabilities.description: A standalone, session-based development app — 'Mission Control' for agentic work — with multi-repo sessions, a built-in terminal and browser, and no IDE required.
valueProposal: **Unified Agentic Workflow:** GitHub Copilot app provides a native desktop experience that consolidates issues, pull requests, repositories, and agent sessions into a single, focused workflow, reducing context switching and accelerating progress from task to merged PR.

**Parallel Agent Session Management:** The app enables developers to run multiple isolated agent workspaces concurrently, each backed by git worktrees, allowing safe parallel workstreams without interference.

**Seamless Integration with GitHub Workflows:** It keeps agent-driven work connected to existing GitHub systems of record for planning, collaboration, review, validation, and merge, supporting trusted delivery workflows and governance.

**Automated Pull Request Follow-Through:** Features like Agent Merge help reduce manual toil by autonomously managing PR lifecycle tasks such as addressing review feedback, fixing CI failures, and merging when ready.

capabilities.name: Copilot Canvases
capabilities.description: Guided, customizable UI surfaces in the GitHub Copilot App for collaborating with agents (e.g. an issue-readiness analyzer). (Build 2026)
valueProposal: **Guided Collaboration with Agents:** Copilot Canvases provide a structured, visual interface for developers to interact with agents, making it easier to analyze issues, plan work, and execute tasks collaboratively.

**Customizable Workflows for Teams:** Teams can create tailored canvases that align with their specific processes and workflows, enhancing productivity and ensuring that agentic workflows are effectively integrated into team practices.

capabilities.name: Copilot CLI
capabilities.description: Copilot in the terminal — agentic coding outside the IDE, including parallel/fleet execution of subagents.
valueProposal: Brings AI-powered coding assistance directly to the terminal, enabling developers to delegate coding tasks asynchronously while working locally, which boosts productivity and reduces context switching
Helps developers stay in the flow by maintaining persitent context across multi-step workflows
Enables advanced agentic orchestration, such as running multiple subagents in parallel to handle complex tasks, turning manual work into scalable workflows
Deep GitHub integration with repos, issues and PRs, including issue-context handoff to cloud sessions.

capabilities.name: Copilot CLI Cloud Sessions
capabilities.description: Cloud-executed Copilot CLI sessions (sandboxes) that persist after the local CLI is closed, with issue-context handoff. (Build 2026 preview)
valueProposal: Secure and isolated execution environments for GitHub Copilot, allowing Copilot to safely interqact with code, tols filesystem and network resources
Will allow for a Governance- and security layer with firewalls and policies in the future, enabling organizations to more tightly control and monitor Copilot's actions
Decouples the runtime from the developers machine, allowing agents to continue to work on tasks even after the local CLI is closed and providing elastic and scalable compute

capabilities.name: Ralph Loop (Autonomous Iteration)
capabilities.description: A custom-agent loop that autonomously iterates over a task (e.g. raising test coverage) until a goal is met, spawning fresh subagents each pass.
valueProposal: Keep context tight through fresh iterations to avoid polluting the context window.
Complete control with the ability to stop the loop at any time.
Hand off work to the cloud or continue in the background.

capabilities.name: Copilot Code Review (CCR)
capabilities.description: AI code review on pull requests that runs in Actions, uses the Code Graph plus tools (CodeQL, ESLint), and can hand findings to a Coding Agent.
valueProposal: Accelerates the code review process by automatically generating detailed, context-aware review comments,
Integrates seamlessly with existing pull request workflows, reducing manual effort and enabling faster feedback cycle
Enhances collaboration by providing consistent and objective insights, supporting teams in maintaining high standards and reducing review bottlenecks
Leverages AI to understand code context deeply, allowing it to suggest improvements that align with project conventions and best practices

capabilities.name: Copilot Group Changes in PRs
capabilities.description: Copilot automatically groups related file changes in a pull request into logical sections.
valueProposal: Make large PRs easier to review and understand by allowing developers to review related changes together in a focused way, rather than being overwhelmed by a long list of individual file changes

capabilities.name: Copilot Cloud Agent (CCA)
capabilities.description: GitHub Copilot cloud agent is GitHub’s autonomous, asynchronous software engineering agent. It helps developers delegate work to Copilot so they can keep projects moving while staying in control of review, validation, and merge decisions.
valueProposal: **Increase engineering capacity:** Developers can hand off routine, repetitive, or well-scoped tasks while they focus on higher-complexity work.
**Move faster with control:** Copilot can research, plan, code, validate, and request review while keeping humans in the loop.
**Scale agentic workflows:** Teams can automate recurring tasks such as issue triage, failing test fixes, release-note preparation, and repository maintenance.

**Reduce context switching:** Developers can invoke or monitor the agent from the surfaces where they already work, including GitHub.com, Copilot Chat, GitHub Mobile, Raycast, Visual Studio, and the GitHub Copilot app.
**Support enterprise adoption:** Admins have more controls for enablement, runners, secrets, variables, validation tools, and organization-level rollout.

capabilities.name: Copilot Plan Mode
capabilities.description: A Copilot Chat mode that structures and decomposes complex work into an interactive plan before any code is written.
valueProposal: **Increases Context Efficiency & Agent Quality** - Structures complex work and catches architectural decisions early, before a line of code is written, improving the qualiy of downstream agents.
**Interactive Planning** - Planning becomes a first-class, interactive artifact (to-do items with live spinners and checkmarks) rather than a throwaway markdown file.
**Decomposes Work** - Decomposes a vague idea into structured, parallelizable workstreams ready for execution.

capabilities.name: Copilot Vision
capabilities.description: Copilot's ability to read images — design mockups, sketches, screenshots — and translate them into code or structured work items.
valueProposal: Bridges PM and Engineering: a mockup's annotations and engineering notes flow straight into generated issues, reducing back-and-forth.

capabilities.name: Copilot Subagents
capabilities.description: A parent agent that invokes specialized subagents in parallel, each in its own fresh context, to keep the main context tight.
valueProposal: Keep context tight through subagents and fresh iterations so the main context window stays clean.
Run specialized agents in parallel on independent threads (e.g. one test-writer per untested route).

capabilities.name: Copilot Voice
capabilities.description: Voice interaction/dictation within Copilot App features
valueProposal: Interact with Copilot more easily and naturally through dictation, speeding up especially long or complex prompts
Makes Copilot more accessible to developers with disabilities or those who prefer voice input over typing

capabilities.name: Copilot Custom Agents
capabilities.description: Repository- or enterprise-defined agents (`.github/agents/*.md`) scoped to a single responsibility, usable with little prompting.
valueProposal: Encode domain knowledge and team or project specific context and expertise into reusable agents
Allows to turn repeated tasks and patterns into consistent, reviewable workflows
Natively integrated and easily invokable by any Copilot surface

capabilities.name: Copilot Custom Instructions
capabilities.description: Repository configuration (`.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `*.instructions.md`) that personalizes Copilot for internal libraries, standards, and conventions.
valueProposal: Equips Copilot with the "must-know" information at each and every interaction natively and automatically
Allows to tune all Agentic Workflows to the specifics of a project, team, or organization, creating a written contract between humans and agents
Type once, reuse everywhere: Works cross-surface and in all Copilot Experiences - IDE, CLI, App and Code Review.

capabilities.name: Copilot Custom Prompts
capabilities.description: Reusable prompt files (`.github/prompts/*.prompt.md`) that encode repeatable, standardized AI workflows invokable with `/name`.
valueProposal: Codify repetitive propmts and workflows into reusable files that can be invoked by anyone in the repo

capabilities.name: MCP Servers
capabilities.description: Model Context Protocol support that extends Copilot with external tools (local or remote servers).
valueProposal: Extend Copilot's capabilities using the open MCP server protocol - add tools and resources.
Allows to integrate Copilot with internal- or 3rd party tools, providing tailored access to knowledge, APIs and services.
Centralised allowlisting and configuration give teams control over which tools agents can use.

capabilities.name: Playwright MCP
capabilities.description: The Playwright MCP server is integrated by default into CCA and CCR, allowing Copilot to drive the browser and assist in Web Development scenarios.
valueProposal: Built into CCA and CCR by default to allow to drive Browser-interactions more natively and wihtout effort
Especially useful in Web development projets, where Copilot can start and inspect the app easily

capabilities.name: Rubber Duck Review
capabilities.description: A review subagent that uses a different model to give a complementary perspective on a plan or change. (Build 2026)
valueProposal: Multi-model choice: using a different model improves the quality of outputs by providing complementary perspectives.
Provides a competitive differentiator for Copilot, as only few other AI coding assistants have multi-model support.

capabilities.name: Agent Skills
capabilities.description: Portable skill definitions (`.github/skills/*/SKILL.md`) that encode specific knowledge/patterns and load into context only when relevant.
valueProposal: Encode institutional knowledge so code generation is consistent and bespoke, even for new developers or agents.
Increase context efficiency as skills are only loaded on demand
Works across all Copilot surfaces (IDE, CLI, App, Code Review) and can be shared across repos and organizations

capabilities.name: Copilot Agent Hooks
capabilities.description: Lifecycle hooks (`.github/hooks/hooks.json`) that run scripts on agent events for extensibility — audit logging, auto-commits, linting and more.
valueProposal: Enhances productivity and efficiency by seamlessly extending Copilot's capabilities with custom scripts
Brings deterministic, auditable, and automated actions to agentic development

capabilities.name: Mission Control
capabilities.description: A user-level hub (github.com/copilot/agents) that shows all ongoing agent tasks and lets you start, steer, and switch between sessions.
valueProposal: Manage many coding agents at once — kick off, monitor live progress, and steer mid-session from a single pane.
Provides a live view into the commands, MCP servers, and steps an agent is taking, plus the files it changed.
Jump directly from a session to its PR or Codespace to finalise the work.

capabilities.name: Copilot Agent Automations
capabilities.description: Personal, locally-executed recurring AI automations in the Copilot App that combine org knowledge (Spaces) with repo context. (Build 2026)
valueProposal: **Reduced Burden to Entry**: Let anyone — PMs, compliance officers, designers — set up recurring AI-powered processes, not just developers.
**Easy Setup and Maintenance**: Personal and local, making them secure and easy to configure compared with project-level CI/CD automations.

capabilities.name: Copilot Plugins Marketplace
capabilities.description: A marketplace to discover, install, and manage Copilot plugins/MCP extensions across VS Code and the CLI.
valueProposal: Single place to discover community and first-party tools that integrate directly into the AI workflow.
Tailor the AI assistant to a team's toolchain across both VS Code and the CLI.
Plugins like Accessibility provide immediate, visible value by auditing UI components.

capabilities.name: Copilot Agent Mode
capabilities.description: Agentic Copilot Chat inside the IDE that reads the codebase, plans, and makes multi-file changes, validating and self-healing as it goes.
valueProposal: Understands an existing codebase and makes complex, multi-file changes from natural language.
Convention-aware: reads existing patterns (Tailwind, dark mode, config, tests) and generates code that fits in.
Generates tests, runs them, self-heals on errors, and analyses coverage.
Reviewable like a human PR — you can inspect and adjust before accepting.

capabilities.name: Agent Merge
capabilities.description: An agent that automatically drives a PR toward merge-readiness by incorporating review comments, security findings, and CI/CD results.
valueProposal: Automatically fixes CI/CD failures, Copilot Code Review comments, and CodeQL findings without manual intervention.
Removes the toil so human review is genuinely valuable — not rubber-stamping formatting fixes.

capabilities.name: Copilot Spaces
capabilities.description: Copilot Spaces lets developers organize and centralize relevant content—like repositories, code, pull requests, issues, free-text content like transcripts or notes, images, and file uploads—into “spaces” that ground Copilot’s responses in the right context for a specific task.
valueProposal: **Smarter, Context-Aware AI:** Copilot gives better answers grounded in real project context.
**Improved Team Productivity:** Spaces help teams stay aligned and reduce redundant questions.
**Faster Onboarding & Ramp:** New developers get up to speed quickly with curated Spaces.
**Scalable Knowledge Sharing:** Reduce reliance on tribal knowledge and SME bottlenecks.
**Accelerated Delivery:** Developers spend less time searching and more time building.

capabilities.name: Dependabot Alerts
capabilities.description: Surfaces known vulnerabilities in dependencies with advisory metadata (EPSS, CWE).
valueProposal: **Swift Threat Detection & Prioritization** - Surfaces known third-party vulnerabilities the moment they are discovered, with rich advisory metadata to prioritise remediation.

**Unified Supply-Chain Visibility** - Unifies the view of supply-chain vulnerabilities across the repository and all projects in an organization, including those in private repos, and provides a single source of truth for security teams.

capabilities.name: Dependabot Version Updates
capabilities.description: Automated pull requests that update outdated dependencies and base images.
valueProposal: **Decrease Mental Load & Toil work** - Updates are toil work which dependabot removes entirely, decreasing the mental load of developers and security teams, and allowing them to focus on higher-value work.

**Native GitHub Experience** - Dependabot is built into GitHub, surfacing PRs and alerts in the same place as other code changes, and integrates with existing workflows for review, validation, and merge.

capabilities.name: Dependency Review
capabilities.description: A required workflow that checks dependency changes in a PR for vulnerabilities and license violations and blocks the merge.
valueProposal: **Shift Supply-Chain Security Left** - Dependency Review prevents developers from introducing supply-chain vulnerabilities early and as a standard part of the PR review process, rather than relying on security teams to triage and remediate after the fact.

capabilities.name: Repository Rulesets
capabilities.description: Branch/repo rules (PRs required, code scanning, required workflows) applied dynamically, including by custom-property metadata.
valueProposal: **Enterprise-Scale Governance:** Apply consistent policies in a single place, applied across all repositories, ensuring compliance and security.

**Flexible and Dynamic Policy Application:** Use custom properties or other filters to dynamically apply rulesets based on repository metadata, allowing for tailored governance that adapts to different project needs.
**Bypass and Override Capabilities:** Allow for guided exceptions or overrides in specific cases, providing flexibility while maintaining overall governance standards.
**Insightful Reporting and Auditing:** Gain visibility into policy enforcement and compliance status across the organization, enabling proactive management and auditing of repository governance.

capabilities.name: Custom Properties
capabilities.description: Repository metadata used to classify repos and drive dynamic policy (e.g. which rulesets apply).
valueProposal: **Dynamic & Flexible Repository Metadata:** Custom properties allow organizations to classify repositories based on specific criteria, enabling more granular control over governance policies.

capabilities.name: Actions Allow List
capabilities.description: Repository/org policy that restricts which GitHub Actions may run, blocking unapproved or vulnerable actions.
valueProposal: **Safe & Secure Open Source Action Usage:** Mitigates supply chain risks by preventing the use of unapproved or untrusted actions
**Improved Governance and Auditability:** Helps with governance and auditability by providing a clear record of allowed actions

capabilities.name: Artifact Attestations
capabilities.description: Cryptographically verifiable build provenance and SBOMs generated in Actions and verified before deployment.
valueProposal: Provide verifiable, tamper-proof build metadata to improve security and compliance.
Offer a simple way to confirm an artifact's integrity before deployment.

capabilities.name: Virtual Registry / Linked Artifacts
capabilities.description: Links published artifacts to deployment context so security alerts can be prioritized by real production exposure.
valueProposal: Visibility and traceability into which artifacts are deployed where, and which versions are in production, helps with compliance and auditing.
Associating production/deployment context with alerts prioritises by real risk, reducing noise and focusing on what's exposed.

capabilities.name: Copilot AI Controls (Control Plane)
capabilities.description: Enterprise control plane unifying Copilot/agent policies, agent sessions, audit logs, and MCP allowlists.
valueProposal: **Accelerate Innovation, Minimize Risk:** The Agent Control Plane empowers teams to move quickly with agentic automation, while enterprise owners retain control over policy, configuration, and oversight.

**Balance Developer Freedom with Governance:** When paired with Mission Control, enterprises achieve the ideal balance—empowering developers to innovate while maintaining enterprise-grade security, compliance, and operational control.
**Future-Ready Platform:** Lays the foundation for scaling agentic activity to thousands of specialized agents, enabling organizations to confidently adopt autonomous workflows and maximize ROI.

capabilities.name: Custom Agent Rulesets
capabilities.description: Enterprise rulesets that standardize and control where custom agents may be generated and used.
valueProposal: Standardize custom agents across the enterprise with centralized configuration.
Control custom-agent generation via rulesets — allow specific orgs/repos or disable entirely.

capabilities.name: MCP Policy Controls
capabilities.description: Enterprise-wide MCP allowlisting and registry configuration enforced across IDEs.
valueProposal: Set an enterprise MCP allowlist so only validated MCP connections are permitted when developers use agents.
Centralized policy enforcement across IDEs (VS Code today, GitHub.com coming).

capabilities.name: Issues
capabilities.description: Issue tracking with types (Epic/Feature/Task), hierarchical sub-issues, blocking dependencies, and PR linkage.
valueProposal: Organize, plan and track work easily and natively integrated
Brings project management capabilities into GitHub

capabilities.name: Agent Automation Controls in GitHub Issues
capabilities.description: Review controls for issue changes proposed by agent automations, including approvals, confidence levels, and rationale.
valueProposal: **Human control:** Hold suggested issue changes for review and accept or decline them individually or in bulk.
**Confidence-based automation:** Use agent confidence and repository thresholds to decide which changes apply automatically and which require review.
**Transparent decisions:** Record rationale for supported actions so maintainers can understand what changed and why without adding triage comments.

capabilities.name: Issue Fields (Org-Level Custom Metadata)
capabilities.description: Organization-level custom issue fields (e.g. Severity, Root Cause, Affected Users) for consistent categorization across repos.
valueProposal: Engineering orgs need consistent incident categorization.
Org-level fields make every repo report incidents the same way — no per-repo setup, no inconsistent labeling.

capabilities.name: Projects (Boards, Fields, Views)
capabilities.description: Project boards with custom fields and multiple views (backlog, sprint board, roadmap) for agile planning.
valueProposal: **Integrated Planning & Tracking:** GitHub Projects provides a unified system to connect work items directly to code changes, enabling teams to track progress and link development work to requirements.
**Workflow Customization & Organization:** It allows establishing conventions for issue templates, labeling, and project organization tailored to team workflows, enhancing clarity and efficiency.

**Single Source of Truth:** By integrating planning and development, GitHub Projects creates a centralized source where stakeholders can monitor project status and developers can align work with goals.

**Enhanced Collaboration & Visibility:** The platform supports collaboration through transparent tracking and linking of issues, pull requests, and project tasks, improving communication and accountability.

capabilities.name: Project Automations
capabilities.description: Built-in project workflows that automate item management (auto-add, auto-archive, auto-close, on-merge).
valueProposal: Automate common project-management tasks (auto-add items/sub-issues, auto-archive, auto-close, react to merges) improves efficiency and reduces manual overhead, allowing teams to focus on high-value work.

capabilities.name: Microsoft Foundry
capabilities.description: A managed Azure platform for building, deploying, and grounding AI agents — combining model hosting, vector search, and the Responses API in a single portal.
valueProposal: **No-code agent authoring** — define a system prompt, attach grounding documents via File Search, and publish an API endpoint without writing infrastructure code.
**Grounded, trustworthy responses** — retrieval-augmented generation over uploaded knowledge bases prevents hallucinated facts, discounts, or policies.
**Secure by default** — integrates with Azure RBAC and `DefaultAzureCredential`; no long-lived secrets required in application code.
**Playground for rapid iteration** — test agent behavior in the Foundry UI before wiring it to a frontend, enabling fast prompt and grounding tuning.

capabilities.name: Pull Request Stacks
capabilities.description: Related pull requests can be organized into a dependency stack, making it easier to build, review, and update a larger change as a sequence of focused contributions.
valueProposal: Keep dependent work reviewable in smaller, ordered pull requests instead of one large change.
Make dependencies between pull requests visible and keep upper pull requests aligned when a lower pull request changes.
Support incremental review and validation, with CI running against each layer of the stack.

capabilities.name: Secret Scanning
capabilities.description: Detection of committed credentials across the full Git history, including AI-detected generic secrets, with rich remediation metadata.
valueProposal: **Become more secure:** Prevent, detect, and remediate secret leaks - the number one cause of security incidents in software development.

**Native Integration:** Secret Protection integrates seamlessly into developer workflows, enabling more secure software development with less disruption to velocity, and it provides tools that enable quick and efficient remediation.

**Easy Adoption & Standardized Processes:** For security teams, Secret Protection helps eliminate the need to adopt and manage additional tools, offering increased visibility into and alignment with developer processes.

**Proactive Prevention:** By combining proactive prevention–such as blocking secrets before they are committed–with low false-positive rates, Secret Protection minimizes the risk of unauthorized access to sensitive systems.

**Enterprise Governance at Scale:** Scans repositories, pull requests, issue comments, wikis, discussions, gists, and Git history to help identify exposed secrets wherever they occur across the development lifecycle.

capabilities.name: Push Protection
capabilities.description: Blocks commits containing detected secrets before they are pushed.
valueProposal: Prevents accidental secret commits from reaching the remote in the first place.

capabilities.name: Repository Security Overview
capabilities.description: Per-repository consolidated view of all active CodeQL, Dependabot, and Secret Scanning alerts on the main branch.
valueProposal: **Developer-Facing Risk Snapshot:** Gives individual repo owners a single security tab to triage all alert types without switching tools.
**Actionable at the Source:** Surfaced directly in the repository context, making it easy for developers to own and remediate their own risks.
**Supercharged with AI:** Helps developer in cleanup motions through Copilot Autofix and capabilities to assign alerts to Copilot Cloud Agent for an easy fix.

capabilities.name: Organization Security Overview
capabilities.description: Org-level dashboard aggregating CodeQL, Dependabot, and Secret Scanning alerts across all repositories, with risk trends and remediation progress.
valueProposal: **Unified Security Visibility:** Single pane of glass across all GHAS alert types for the entire organization, eliminating per-repo navigation.
**Risk Prioritization:** Filtered views and trend data help security teams identify the most critical exposures and track remediation progress over time.
**Evidence of Security Posture:** Demonstrate measurable improvement in security posture to auditors and leadership using trend charts and coverage metrics.

capabilities.name: Enterprise Security Overview
capabilities.description: Enterprise-wide aggregation of security alerts across all organizations, enabling security leaders to track posture, coverage, and remediation at scale.
valueProposal: **Cross-Org Visibility at Scale:** Roll up CodeQL, Dependabot, and Secret Scanning signals across every organization in the enterprise into a single dashboard.
**Strategic Risk Management:** Identify which organizations or repository clusters carry the highest security debt, enabling targeted remediation investments.
**Compliance Reporting:** Provide auditors and CISOs with a unified, up-to-date view of security coverage and open vulnerabilities across the entire software estate.

walkthroughs.title: Creating the Attestation
walkthroughs.content:
1. In the demo repository, navigate to the **Actions** tab and select **Attestations**.
  ![Screenshot showing the Actions tab with Attestations menu item highlighted in the left sidebar](./images/attestation-navigation.png)
2. You will find at least four attestations (two each for the frontend and API). Focus on the API attestations and their distinct `predicate-types`:

    ![Screenshot displaying a list of artifact attestations showing different predicate types for frontend and API containers](./images/attestation-types.png)

    1. `https://spdx.dev/Document/v2.3`: Confirms an SBOM is attached. (Note: This does not validate the SBOM's contents).
    2. `https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1`: Verifies the artifact's origin, confirming it was built by a specific reusable workflow and originated from your demo repository.
3. Return to the [Build and Publish](../../.github/workflows/build-and-publish.yml) workflow (accessible via the `Workflow File` link on the attestation page).
4. Point out that this workflow uses a reusable workflow to generate attestations, and navigate to it: https://github.com/octobooth-demos/octocat-supply-reusable-workflows/blob/main/.github/workflows/build-publish-containers.yml
5. In the reusable workflow, scroll to the bottom to show the simple, built-in actions that generate the attestations.
  ![Screenshot of workflow YAML file showing the steps that generate SBOM and SLSA attestations using GitHub Actions](./images/attestation-workflow-file.png)

walkthroughs.title: Verifying the Attestation
walkthroughs.content:
1. In a local checkout or Codespace, open a terminal.
2. Run the verification script:

    ```bash
    ./demo/resources/verify-attestation.sh
    ```

3. The output will show:
  ![Terminal output showing successful verification of artifact attestations with SLSA provenance and SBOM checks](./images/attestation-cli-output.png)
    1. The raw output from the `gh attestation verify` command.
    2. A summary explaining the verification results.

4. (Optional) If Azure deployments are configured, show how verification can be enforced in a GitHub Action:
    1. Open the deployment workflow: [.github/workflows/deploy.yml](../../.github/workflows/deploy.yml).
    2. Open the `Verify Container Attestations` step.
    3. Navigate to the custom action's source: [.github/actions/verify-container-attestations/action.yml](../../.github/actions/verify-container-attestations/action.yml).
    4. The `GH_COMMAND` environment variable contains the `gh attestation verify` commands for both SLSA and SBOM checks.
    5. This action also generates a helpful job summary, which you can display by navigating to a successful workflow run.

walkthroughs.title: Virtual Registry, aka Linked Artifacts
walkthroughs.content:
1. After repository creation, wait for the deployment action to complete.
2. Navigate to the [organization's Linked artifacts page](https://github.com/orgs/octobooth-demos/artifacts).

    ![Screenshot showing the Linked Artifacts page in a GitHub organization](./images/linked-artifacts-overview.png)

3. In the linked artifacts, search for the `api` artifact of your repository:

    ```txt
    octobooth-demos/-api
    ```

4. Review the information on this screen:
    ![Screenshot showing the details page of Linked Artifacts](./images/linked-artifacts-details.png)
    1. **Source Repository:** This links this metadata record to the actual source repository. In the demo's case, this is automatically done through the provenance attestation created during the build process (see the [Artifact Attestations](#artifact-attestations) section above).
    2. **Attestations:** A list of all associated attestations is also provided at the bottom of the page.
    3. **Storage Record:** This links the artifact itself to this metadata record.
    4. **Deployments:** This is the main piece. Here, metadata about the deployment of the artifact in production can be added, such as the cluster name, risk metadata (like `internet-exposed`), physical location, etc.

5. Go to the `Organization's Security Page` -> `Alerts (Section Header)` -> `Code Scanning`.
6. Apply the two filters `runtime-risk:internet-exposed` and `severity:high` (optionally, if there are too many results in your demo organization, add a filter for the repository name `repo:octobooth-demos/`).
7. You should see the alert `SQL query built from user-controlled sources` in the list with the `internet-exposed` runtime risk filter applied.
    1. (optional): Use this direct link to the filtered view: <https://github.com/orgs/octobooth-demos/security/alerts/code-scanning?query=is%3Aclosed+runtime-risk%3Ainternet-exposed+severity%3Ahigh++repo%3A>

8. Review the autofix suggestions provided by Copilot in the comment.
9. Show the available options: commit the suggestion to the PR, dismiss the finding, or reply to the autofix.

walkthroughs.title: Demo: Custom Agents Driving a Multi-Phase Workflow
walkthroughs.content:
1. **Plan the Feature (Plan Mode):**
     - In VSCode, open Copilot Chat and switch to **Plan** mode (or use `/plan` in the CLI)
     - Enter the prompt:

       ```prompt
       I want a new method that gets the orders for a branch ID
       ```
     - Walk through the planning conversation — Copilot will ask clarifying questions and produce a structured plan
     - Once satisfied, keep the plan open — it serves as input for the agents in the next phases

     > [!TIP]
     > See the [Planning Mode in VSCode](#planning-mode-in-vscode-copilot-) section below for a detailed walkthrough of Plan mode.

  2. **🔴 Red Phase — `tdd-red` Agent:**
     - Switch to the `tdd-red` agent from the agents dropdown
     - Prompt it with a single requirement from the plan, e.g.:

       ```prompt
       Write a failing test for getting orders by branch ID
       ```
     - Show how the agent is **constrained by its prompt** — it writes a test but refuses to write implementation code
     - Show the test output confirming the test fails (e.g., HTTP 404 — route not implemented)

  3. **🟢 Green Phase — `tdd-green` Agent:**
     - Switch to the `tdd-green` agent
     - Prompt:

       ```prompt
       Make the failing test pass
       ```
     - Show how this agent's scope is different — it reads existing tests and writes only enough implementation to make them pass
     - Show the test passing ✅

  4. **🔵 Blue Phase — `tdd-blue` Agent:**
     - Switch to the `tdd-blue` agent
     - Prompt:

       ```prompt
       Refactor the implementation while keeping tests green
       ```
     - Show how this agent focuses on code quality — refactoring, naming, documentation — while continuously running tests to prevent regressions

  5. **Repeat the Cycle:**
     - Go back to `tdd-red` for the next requirement from the plan
     - Cycle through Red → Green → Blue to show how agents hand off context through the code itself (tests, implementation, plan)

  6. **Key Points to Highlight:**
     - **Role-Scoped Agents**: Each agent has strict boundaries — Red won't implement, Green won't refactor, Blue won't add features
     - **Developer-Driven Orchestration**: The developer decides when to switch agents — there's no magic; the workflow is transparent
     - **Context Through Code**: Agents hand off context via the artifacts they produce (tests, implementation, plan doc) — not hidden state
     - **Prompt Engineering in Practice**: Open `.github/agents/` to show how each agent's prompt enforces its role and constraints
     - **Reusable Pattern**: This same multi-agent pattern applies to any phased workflow (e.g., design → implement → review)

  7. **(Optional) Show the Agent Configuration:**
     - Open `.github/agents/` to show the three TDD agents and their prompt files:
       - `tdd-red.agent.md`: Scoped to writing failing tests only
       - `tdd-green.agent.md`: Scoped to minimal implementation
       - `tdd-blue.agent.md`: Scoped to refactoring with tests green
     - Highlight how each agent's system prompt is what enforces the constraints you just saw in action

   - You can see elapsed time per agent.
   - Each agent works independently -- no conflicts during development thanks to worktrees.

walkthroughs.title: Demo: Orchestrate Dependent Work as a Pull Request Stack
walkthroughs.prep: Make sure the `orchestrate` and `gh-stack` skills are enabled in the GitHub Copilot App.
walkthroughs.content:
1. Open the pre-seeded [Show product stock levels and low-stock warnings](../../inventory.md) issue in the Copilot App and start a coordinating session from it. Explain the database → API → frontend work order from its description. The three task issues are standalone (not linked as sub-issues or issue dependencies); open them individually as needed.
2. Ask Copilot to coordinate the work as a PR stack:

   ```prompt
   Starting from the latest main, use `/orchestrate` and the `gh-stack` skill to implement the feature issue and its three standalone task issues as a PR stack. Read the task issue requirements and implement them in this order:

   - Database: "Persist product stock quantities and seed demo inventory".
   - API: "Expose product stock quantities through the API", after Database.
   - Frontend: "Display product stock quantities and availability warnings", after API.

   Create one Copilot App session and one PR per task issue. Each session owns its branch and changes, validates its layer, commits, pushes, and opens its PR before the next layer starts from that branch. Target main for the database PR and the layer below for each upper PR. Register and verify the PRs as one GitHub stack, and give each PR a concise description linking its task issue.

   Do not merge the PRs. When the stack is ready, show the session chain, PR links, and GitHub stack view.
   ```

3. Explain why `/orchestrate` fits this scenario: the three layers cannot all start as independent implementation tasks at the outset, so their branches and PRs follow the stated order. Independent preparation, such as code exploration or test planning, can still run in parallel; `/fleet` is useful for independent tasks, but is not the main story here. While the agents work, show the sessions appearing in the app and explain the ownership chain: each session has its own worktree and branch, and each upper layer is based on the layer below it. Switch between sessions to show that you can monitor and manage the work from one place.
4. When the PRs are ready, open the stack on GitHub.com. Show the dependency order, each focused diff, and the checks running for each layer. Explain that stacked PRs let reviewers validate incremental changes without waiting for one oversized PR.
5. **Optional follow-up — change the bottom PR and rebase:** In the coordinating session, ask the agent to change one seeded product's stock from a low-stock value (1–5) to `6` in the database PR only. Ask it to push the change and stop:

   ```prompt
   In the database PR's session, change one seeded product's stock quantity from a low-stock value (1–5) to 6. Keep the change in the database layer only. Push it, then stop. Do not rebase or merge the stack.
   ```
6. In the stack worktree, check out the bottom PR's branch and run `gh stack rebase --upstack`, then run `gh stack submit` to push the updated stack. Return to the stack on GitHub.com to show that the upper PRs are based on the updated bottom PR and their CI checks run again.
7. Recap the two complementary ideas: the Copilot App orchestrates isolated sessions for dependent work, while GitHub keeps the PR stack connected and makes updating the upper layers manageable. Leave the PRs open and do not merge them.

walkthroughs.title: Automated Workflow: Compliance Check
walkthroughs.content:
1. **Navigate to Workflows** in the GitHub Copilot App.
2. **Create a new workflow:**
   - **Name:** `OctoCAT Supply Compliance Review`
   - **Project:** Select your demo repository
   - **Mode:** Autopilot (so it runs without intervention)
   - **Model:** Choose your preferred model (e.g., Claude Opus for best results -- "we're going to burn through tokens")
   - **Prompt:**

     ```prompt
     Get the contents of the Copilot Space "OD OctoCAT Supply Compliance Docs".

     Using those compliance requirements as your reference, perform a thorough compliance assessment of this repository. Check:
     - Are all required legal pages (Privacy Policy, Terms of Service, Cookie Banner) implemented?
     - Does the application meet data handling and storage requirements?
     - Are there any gaps between what compliance requires and what is currently implemented?

     Generate a detailed report as a GitHub Issue with:
     - A summary of the compliance status (pass/fail per category)
     - Specific gaps found, with references to both the compliance docs and the codebase
     - Recommended next steps, prioritized by severity

     Title the issue "[Compliance] Repository Assessment - <today's date>"
     ```

3. **Create the workflow and trigger it** manually.
4. **While it runs (~1-2 minutes)**, explain the key narrative:
   - The workflow uses the GitHub MCP to access the Copilot Space, download the compliance docs, and understand the organizational standards.
   - **Workflows vs. Agentic Workflows**: Workflows in the GitHub Copilot App are **personal, locally-executed automations** -- they run on your machine using your local Copilot CLI. This means they use your local authentication (no secrets to expose in a shared repo). Agentic Workflows (GitHub Actions) are project-level automations that run in the cloud.
   - **Show the Copilot Space**: Navigate to github.com/copilot/spaces > Organizations > Octodemo > "OD OctoCAT Supply Compliance Docs". Explain: "Imagine this is the central space for all things privacy, compliance, and security -- the organization's guidelines and standards."
   - This could run on a schedule (e.g., every Friday) to continuously validate compliance.
   - Other use cases: weekly activity snippet reports, documentation freshness checks, dependency audits.
5. **Show the results** (use a pre-completed run if the live one isn't done):
   - Navigate to Workflows, select a previous run to show the output.
   - Open the generated **GitHub Issue** with the compliance assessment report.
   - Walk through the findings -- highlight how it references specific compliance documents from the Space and maps them to actual code in the repo.
   - Show the overall status: the demo repo typically shows gaps (not fully compliant), making it a realistic scenario.
6. **(Optional) Close the loop**: From the compliance report, prompt the agent to derive a plan to address the findings and create issues for each gap. This demonstrates going from assessment to remediation using the same tool.

walkthroughs.title: Act 1 — Build the Brain (Microsoft Foundry)
walkthroughs.prep: Azure Foundry project with `Azure AI User` role; active `az login` session in terminal. Can be pre-staged before the live demo.
walkthroughs.content:
1. **Install dependencies** (if not already done):

   ```bash
   make install
   ```

2. **Start the app** (if not already running):

   ```bash
   make dev
   ```

3. **Walk through the homepage** — show the basic homepage, product catalog, etc.
4. **Click into a product** — show the current product details experience before adding the chatbot.
5. **Open Microsoft Foundry** — navigate to [ai.azure.com](https://ai.azure.com) and log in. Create a new project (or use an existing one). You'll need to specify your Azure subscription, resource group, name, and region.

   ![Create Foundry Project](./images/foundry-create-project.png)

   > [!NOTE]
   > This step takes a few minutes. You can pre-stage it to save time and avoid capacity issues inside Azure.

   > [!TIP]
   > The `Azure AI User` role should be automatically assigned to you when creating the resource through the Foundry portal. If you run into access issues, check **Access control (IAM)** on the Foundry resource in the **Azure portal**.

6. **Create a new Agent**
   - Click **Build** in the top nav bar
   - Click **Agents** in the left nav
   - Click **Create Agent** in the main pane
   - Give it a name: `OctoCAT-Support-Agent`.

7. **Select the model** — Choose your model. For our demo gpt-4.1 works great, but you can pick any model available in your Foundry instance.

8. **Add the System Prompt**
   - Open `demo/resources/chatbot/system-prompt.md` (or `system-prompt-casual.md` for the fun version) in VS Code.
   - Copy the content and paste it into the **Instructions** field in Foundry.

   > [!TIP]
   > You can later come back and tweak the system prompt if you want to show how changes affect the agent's behavior in real time.

9. **Add a lookup tool**
   - Under the **Tools** section, click **+ Add** → **Browse all Tools** → **File Search** → **Add tool**.
   - Upload `demo/resources/chatbot/agent-grounding.md` as the grounding file.
   - Open the grounding file and point out the catalog, product specs, pricing, inventory status, shipping, returns, warranty, and FAQ policy sections.

   ![Upload Grounding Document](./images/foundry-upload-grounding.png)

   > [!NOTE]
   > The document may take a minute to process. Wait for it to show `Success` before moving on.

   - Click **Attach** to save the tool configuration. Your final agent setup should look like this:

   ![Final Agent Setup](./images/foundry-agent-setup.png)

10. **Test in the Foundry Playground**
    - Use the built-in chat playground to test a few queries:
      - *"What's the best product for a senior cat?"*
      - *"Do you offer free shipping?"*
      - *"My cat was injured by your product"* — should escalate to human support

    ![Foundry Playground Test](./images/foundry-playground-test.png)

11. **Save and Publish the Agent** — once you're satisfied with the behavior, click **Save** and then **Publish** to make it available for API calls.

12. **Note the Agent endpoint** — once published, copy the `Responses API endpoint` URL. You'll need this to connect the frontend chat widget to the agent.

walkthroughs.title: Act 2 — Build the UI (GitHub Copilot: Plan → Agent)
walkthroughs.prep: Act 1 must be completed or pre-staged; Foundry agent endpoint URL must be ready.
walkthroughs.content:
1. **Open Copilot Chat** in VS Code and switch to **Plan** mode.
2. Enter the following prompt:

   ```prompt
   I want to add a customer support chatbot widget to the OctoCAT Supply frontend.

   Requirements:
   - Floating chat bubble in the bottom-right corner of every page
   - Clicking it opens a chat panel with message history
   - Messages are sent to our Microsoft Foundry agent endpoint
   - The widget should match our existing Tailwind design system and support dark mode
   - Include a typing indicator while waiting for the agent response
   - The chat panel should have a close/minimize button

   The agent is already deployed in Microsoft Foundry at <insert endpoint URL here>. Auth should go through a backend proxy route that uses DefaultAzureCredential from @azure/identity with the token scope https://ai.azure.com/.default (this is the correct audience for Foundry application endpoints — NOT cognitiveservices.azure.com). The dev environment has an active az login session that DefaultAzureCredential will pick up.
   ```

   > [!TIP]
   > We're being specific about the auth setup since Copilot tends to get this wrong. It will eventually self-heal but this helps it get it right on the first try.

3. **Walk through the plan** Copilot generates:
   - Point out how it identifies the files to create and modify.
   - Verify that it respects the existing architecture (component structure, Tailwind, dark mode).
   - Note the plan includes things like state management, API integration, and responsive layout.

4. **(Optional) Refine the plan** — answer any follow-up questions Copilot had to refine the plan before committing to implementation.

5. **(Optional) Create a GitHub issue** — if you want to show async handoff, ask Copilot to create a new issue in the repo with the plan details using the GitHub MCP server:

   ```prompt
   This is a new feature request. Please create a GitHub issue in the repo with the implementation plan and steps outlined.
   ```

   Copilot will generate an issue with the plan details. You can then assign it to Copilot or a 3rd party agent to implement asynchronously, or you can take the plan and implement it yourself in real time.
